acceptance: Native Linux cold and warm results recorded with environment and version metadata
Differential validation passes on the same build before timing
context:
Item-specific guardrails: no publication or cross-platform claims without a user decision; no cloud spend without approval.

Shared SereneDB guardrails: worktree-only repository writes with make agent-write-preflight; explicit-path staging, never git add -A; commit identity check, no attribution trailers; uv only, no new dependency; lazy psycopg import; no credentials in Git, logs, fixtures, or tracker; Mocker never in CI and its timings never published; pin by digest or exact version and record version(); announce long runs and never commit raw logs; code-skill self-review then make pr-preflight and make pr-open, no auto-merge without make pr-ready; durable artifacts carry no tracker IDs or session narrative; stop and report on failed gates, unverified behavior, or unapproved host changes.
description:
Mocker timings are indicative only. Produce measured SereneDB performance on a native Linux host using the official tarball or .deb (amd64 or arm64), outside any VM or container runtime overhead.

Tasks:
1. Choose a Linux host. Record CPU, RAM, disk, and kernel. Install the digest-matched SereneDB release (tarball or .deb) and record `serened --version` and version().
2. Protocol: fixed query order and seed; cold run after load, then three warm repetitions with median and spread; explicit `threads` and `memory_limit` settings recorded.
3. TPC-H and TPC-DS at SF 1 and SF 10, with differential validation passing first.
4. Record results with full environment metadata.

Decision gates:
- G1 Start only with explicit user priority and a user-approved host. A cloud host is a live cloud run and needs explicit approval with cost bounds.
- G2 Publishing or comparing results is a separate user decision.
